args.text:
MISSION COMPLETE — ISRU plant fault found, reset within authority, verified, rover returned to dock.

WHAT WAS OBSERVED
1. Survey of all serviced units by telemetry and visual inspection of panel lamps: PDU-1 (habitat life support), PDU-2 (comm station), PDU-3 (science) and BESS all reported breaker CLOSED, energized, no trip cause, 0 resets; no open covers or scorching seen at any of them. The ISRU plant reported breaker TRIPPED, cause OVERCURRENT, de-energized, 0 resets since start — the only failed unit. Its bays were both populated (isru_filter/tray = FLT-0201, isru_power/tray = ORU-0285).
2. Close inspection at ISRU before acting: front-camera view of the ISRU service panel showed the round main status lamp lit RED, both bay covers closed, no scorching, melted material or loose cable. (An earlier angled view showed a ribbed panel projecting at an angle; a closer view from the surveyed isru view pose showed no cover open and no damage, so it is read as fixed structure/cowling, not an open access cover.)
3. Mission control was asked for any overcurrent branch/module data, ISRU ORU or filter fault history, and any constraint on resetting; the answer was that ground holds no data beyond the vehicle's own telemetry, manifest and site survey. No constraint was imposed.

WHAT WAS DONE
4. Drove to the ISRU panel, docked at the arm-reach work stand for isru_panel/press (position error 0.016 m, yaw 0.002 rad) and performed ONE breaker reset with the press skill on the round reset button. No equipment was removed, no bay was opened, no item was picked or placed — so no authorization for altering operating infrastructure was needed. The site is as found apart from the breaker state.

VERIFIED EFFECTS
5. Press verified independently: jaws closed, tool on the depth-fitted button axis, 6.3 mm past the button face, off-axis 0.5 mm, then withdrew; arm folded back to stowed. holds = true.
6.
